references.text: The preceding context where Moses explains that on the sixth day they are to gather twice as much bread, because the seventh day is the Sabbath.
The continuation explaining that they should gather manna for six days, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, there will be none.
The Lord has given the people the Sabbath, and on the seventh day they shall stay at home and rest.
The fourth commandment to keep the Sabbath holy, which is the formal law regarding Sabbath observance.
God rested on the seventh day after creation and sanctified it, which is the theological basis for the Sabbath.
The repetition of the Sabbath command in Deuteronomy, with reference to the exodus from Egypt.
The Sabbath is mentioned as a holy assembly where no work shall be done.
Isaiah speaks of the blessing of keeping the Sabbath holy and calling it a delight.
Nehemiah rebukes the people for profaning the Sabbath by trading and working.
A Sabbath rest remains for God's people, pointing back to the original Sabbath rest.
Direct narrative connection: Both verses are parts of the same event concerning the manna and the Sabbath in the wilderness.
Theological connection: 16:4 introduces the test of daily gathering, while 16:25 specifies the Sabbath rule within this test.
Thematic parallel: Both emphasize the principle of consuming God's gift on the same day and not storing it for the next day.
